questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

It is __easiest__ to stay calm than to protest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. easier .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence **compares two actions:** "staying calm" and "protesting."
 
• In such comparisons, the correct form of the adjective is the **comparative degree**, which is formed by adding "-er" or using "more" before the adjective.
 
• The word "easiest" is in the superlative degree, which is incorrect for this context because it is not comparing more than two actions or things.
 
• The correct comparative form of "easy" is "easier."

Correct sentence: *It is **easier **__to stay calm than to protest.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Degrees of Comparison:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Describes a quality without any comparison. Example: "This is easy."
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Compares two objects, actions, or people. Example: "This is easier than that."
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Compares more than two objects, actions, or people. Example: "This is the easiest task."

• The phrase "knuckle up" is not the correct idiomatic expression. The appropriate phrase is "**knuckle down**," which means to work hard or focus seriously on a task.

• **Option 1: "crack the upcoming deal."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.

__
 
• The word **"thrown out of gear"** refers to something being disrupted, disorganised, or put into a state of confusion. (विस्थापित या गड़बड़ होना)

 
 
• **Example:** The entire schedule was **thrown out of gear** when the train was delayed by two hours.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the idiom "**thrown out of gear**" aptly describes the state of the cottage industries, which are disorganised and struggling due to a lack of finances. (गड़बड़ या अस्त-व्यस्त होना)
 
 
• **Example:** The factory was **thrown out of gear** after the workers went on strike.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 1: Taking somebody for a ride** (किसी को धोखा देना): To deceive or cheat someone.

 
 
• **Example:** The salesman was **taking people for a ride** by selling fake products at high prices.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Worn and torn** (पुराना और घिसा हुआ): Refers to something that is damaged or shabby due to excessive use.
 
 
• **Example:** The **worn and torn** sofa needed to be replaced immediately.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Under a cloud** (संदेह में होना): To be under suspicion or in disgrace.
 
 
• **Example:** The manager was **under a cloud** after accusations of financial fraud were made against him.
